qs.q: A 64-year-old man undergoes complete endoscopic mucosal resection of a 1.2 cm well-differentiated intramucosal gastric adenocarcinoma without lymphovascular invasion. Histopathology confirms clear negative margins. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
o: Perform a positron emission tomography scan
qs.e: Endoscopic surveillance is recommended after complete endoscopic mucosal resection of low-risk mucosal adenocarcinoma to detect local recurrences or metachronous lesions. Prophylactic surgical resection is not indicated because the risk of lymph node metastasis in well-differentiated intramucosal lesions is negligible.
qs.s: Gastric Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Gastrectomy: MCQs
